intro: A 7-day, 6-night first trip through Beijing and Shanghai, with arrival, departure and the intercity journey counted explicitly, plus a faster alternative via Xi'an.
quickAnswer: For a first trip with seven calendar days in China, including arrival on Day 1 and departure on Day 7, start with Beijing and Shanghai: three nights in each city, one intercity journey and six hotel nights in total. Use Days 2–3 for Beijing's imperial centre and Great Wall, Day 4 for the move, and Days 5–6 for Shanghai. Arrival and departure are not full sightseeing days. The three-city version below adds Xi'an at a faster pace; choose it only when your actual flights, trains and attraction bookings fit.

sections.title: 7 days in China means 6 hotel nights

rows: 7 calendar days, arriving Day 1 and leaving Day 7
Use either day-by-day route below; arrival and departure are included
You need additional travel time outside those seven days
Add the extra date explicitly instead of calling it a 7-day, 6-night trip

items: Day 1 means the date you arrive in China, not the date you leave home. Long-haul flights can cross dates; use the local dates on your tickets.
The recommended route has three nights in Beijing and three in Shanghai. Its four main sightseeing days are Days 2, 3, 5 and 6; Day 4 is an intercity travel day.
These are suggested routes, not confirmed transport or admission reservations. Choose the order around actual flights, train availability, attraction bookings and opening days.

sections.title: Choose the right 7-day route

rows: You want the Great Wall, imperial sights and Shanghai with one intercity move
You want slower travel, have return flights to the same city, or prefer fewer hotel changes
The Terracotta Warriors are essential and your live transport times fit the tighter plan

items: For a first visit with seven calendar days, start with the two-city plan. Choose the three-city version only if its extra journey is worth losing recovery time.
Compare flying into Beijing and out of Shanghai, or the reverse. If you must return to the arrival city, allow another travel block and shorten the route.
Check visa or visa-free eligibility against your passport, route, purpose, ports and dates before buying non-refundable transport.

sections.title: Recommended 7-day China itinerary: Beijing and Shanghai

rows: Arrive, transfer to the hotel, set up data and payments, and keep the evening light
Palace Museum / Forbidden City and Jingshan, if your booking and the opening day allow
One Great Wall section with outward and return transport planned
Move from Beijing to Shanghai; allow for checkout, station or airport access, security and hotel check-in
Yu Garden area and the Bund; choose a manageable route and skyline view
Neighbourhoods, a museum, architecture or food; select one nearby day trip only if you prefer it to a city day
Leave time for your actual departure airport and terminal; add a local stop only if the flight time allows

items: Night check: Beijing on Days 1–3 and Shanghai on Days 4–6 gives six hotel nights. Do not add a seventh night unless you also add another calendar date.

The Palace Museum normally closes on Mondays, except statutory holidays. If Day 2 is an ordinary Monday, swap the Palace Museum and Great Wall days, subject to confirmed tickets, safe conditions and opening notices.
Keep Day 4 as a travel block instead of promising a major Beijing attraction before the train. Only add a short local visit after checking the real journey and luggage arrangements.
This version gives Beijing two full sightseeing days. To add a third, move the transfer to Day 5 and accept two Shanghai nights with one full Shanghai day, or extend the trip.

sections.title: Fast alternative: Beijing, Xi'an and Shanghai in 7 days

rows: Arrival, check-in and a short local walk if energy allows
Palace Museum / Forbidden City and Jingshan, arranged around the confirmed booking
Great Wall day trip; keep the evening flexible
Travel to Xi'an; use the remaining time for the City Wall or the Bell and Drum Tower area if the actual train arrival allows
Visit the Terracotta Warriors, then fly to Shanghai only if the museum-to-airport journey and the confirmed flight allow adequate time
Old city or Yu Garden area, the Bund and a skyline view
Airport transfer and departure; any local visit depends on the actual flight time

items: This version has three Beijing nights, one Xi'an night and two Shanghai nights: six in total. It is a fast option with two intercity moves, not the default first-trip recommendation.

Before choosing it, check the Day 4 train and the entire Day 5 chain: museum admission, return transport, luggage collection, airport check-in and the flight. Do not assume a suitable evening flight exists for your date.

If the Day 5 journey does not work, keep a second Xi'an night and reduce Shanghai to one night, extend the trip, or remove a city. Do not keep the original six-night split while adding another hotel stay.
For a history-focused week, Beijing and Xi'an alone may be a better fit. Choose two bases if you have a late arrival, an early departure, children, limited mobility or strong jet lag.

sections.title: Days 1–3: Beijing essentials
items: Keep arrival day light. Immigration, luggage, airport transfer, hotel registration, mobile data, and payment setup can take longer than expected.
Group the Palace Museum and Jingshan as a central sightseeing block. Check Tiananmen-area access separately; a Palace Museum booking does not replace any separate access requirements.
Give the Great Wall a full day. Choose the section, transport, walking difficulty, and return time before departure.
Stay near a useful metro connection, not simply the hotel with the shortest straight-line distance to one attraction.
If the Palace Museum reservation is unavailable, do not buy a suspicious resale ticket; use another imperial-history day and keep checking official information.

sections.title: If you choose the fast route: Xi'an on Days 4–5
items: Use the exact Beijing and Xi'an railway-station names when booking. Both cities have multiple stations and transfer times differ.
A daytime high-speed train is usually the clearest route because it avoids airport transfers and shows how China's rail system works.
Keep the first Xi'an evening flexible. Choose the City Wall or Bell and Drum Tower area based on hotel location and energy.
The Terracotta Warriors are outside central Xi'an. Include round-trip transport, security, entry, and walking time rather than treating the museum as a quick stop.
Before committing to evening travel, check the live schedule and the time needed to collect luggage and reach the airport or station.

sections.title: Shanghai finish: choose stops around your available days
items: Use one day for the contrast between older streets, the Bund, and Pudong rather than crossing the city repeatedly.
On the final day, choose one neighborhood, museum, food area, or missed highlight near a convenient transport route.
Shanghai has two major airports and several railway stations. Confirm the full departure point, terminal, and transfer time.
Do not schedule a distant water town on departure day. Weather, traffic, and return transport can put an international flight at risk.

sections.title: Book these before the trip
items: Open-jaw international flights when possible: arrive in Beijing and depart from Shanghai, or reverse the route if live schedules work better.
Hotels that clearly accept your passport, with the address saved in Chinese and flexible cancellation where practical.
The Palace Museum through its official channel and any other timed Beijing attractions on your final plan.
Terracotta Warriors admission through the official museum channel if you choose the route that includes Xi'an.
Intercity rail or flights when the relevant booking window opens, using the passport name and number exactly.
A working eSIM or roaming plan, Alipay, WeChat, AMap, an offline translation option, and payment backups.

sections.title: Intercity transport decisions
items: Beijing to Xi'an is well suited to high-speed rail. Check the exact live timetable, station, seat class, passport rules, and fare on Railway 12306.
For Xi'an to Shanghai, compare train and flight by door-to-door time—not only the scheduled journey. Include airport transfer, check-in, baggage, and disruption risk.
For Beijing to Shanghai, high-speed rail is often attractive because both city terminals connect to urban transport, but a flight may suit a specific schedule.
Arrive at stations and airports with a realistic buffer. Foreign passports may require a staffed route or additional verification even when e-tickets are used.
Never plan the final long-distance transfer immediately before an international departure without recovery time.

sections.title: What a 7-day China trip may cost
items: Use roughly RMB 350–650 per person per day for a budget planning range, RMB 800–1,500 for mid-range travel, or RMB 1,800–3,000+ for a comfortable style.
These are planning ranges, not fixed prices. International flights and major intercity transport are separate, and peak holidays can change the total substantially.
The three-city itinerary usually costs more than the two-city version because it adds another long journey, hotel change, and local transfer.
Price hotels, 12306 rail tickets or flights, and must-see attractions first; then add food, local transport, data, fees, and a contingency.
For a seven-calendar-day quote, compare six hotel nights separately from daily food and local spending. The broad daily ranges are planning estimates, not an itemised seven-night hotel booking.

links.label: Estimate a 7-day China trip budget
links.description: Choose seven days, group size and travel style; add international flights and intercity travel separately and check hotels for the six actual nights.

sections.title: How to adapt the route
items: History priority: keep Beijing and Xi'an, then fly home from Xi'an instead of adding Shanghai.
Modern cities and easier pacing: use Beijing and Shanghai only, with an optional day trip based on weather and energy.
Food and pandas: replace Shanghai with Chengdu; do not add Chengdu as a fourth city.
Scenery: replace Xi'an or Shanghai with Guilin and Yangshuo, but calculate flight or rail connections before booking.
Limited mobility or children: reduce daily anchors, stay near transport, and preserve a flexible half-day in each base.

sections.title: Common one-week itinerary mistakes
items: Counting arrival and departure as two full sightseeing days after long-haul flights.
Adding four major cities and spending the trip checking out, transferring, and checking in.
Booking a round trip to one city when an open-jaw ticket would remove a costly return journey.
Ignoring exact airport and railway-station names until travel day.
Leaving the Palace Museum, Terracotta Warriors, and peak-date rail bookings until arrival.
Depending on one wallet, one bank card, one map app, or constant internet access.

faqs.question: Is 7 days enough for a trip to China?
faqs.answer: Yes for a focused route. With arrival on Day 1 and departure on Day 7, start with Beijing and Shanghai, three hotel nights in each city and one intercity travel day. The three-city alternative is faster and depends on workable transport.

faqs.question: What is the best 7-day China itinerary for first-time visitors?
faqs.answer: For a first visit with seven calendar days, use Beijing for Days 1–3, move to Shanghai on Day 4, and leave from Shanghai on Day 7. This gives six hotel nights, four main sightseeing days and a travel day, with arrival and departure counted separately from full sightseeing days.

faqs.question: Does a 7-day China itinerary include 7 hotel nights?
faqs.answer: Not when you arrive on Day 1 and leave on Day 7: that is six hotel nights. Seven nights usually span eight calendar dates. Count the local arrival and departure dates on your actual tickets before booking accommodation.

faqs.question: Can I visit Beijing, Xi'an, and Shanghai in one week?
faqs.answer: It can work at a fast pace with three Beijing nights, one Xi'an night and two Shanghai nights. Check that the Terracotta Warriors visit and a suitable onward flight fit Day 5. If they do not, remove a city, reduce Shanghai time or extend the trip.

faqs.question: Should I take trains or flights on this route?
faqs.answer: For Beijing–Shanghai, compare live high-speed train and flight options by total door-to-door time. If adding Xi'an, also check the Beijing–Xi'an train and whether the Day 5 museum visit fits an onward flight. Use exact stations, airports, baggage rules and actual dates.

faqs.question: How much does a 7-day China trip cost?
faqs.answer: A useful daily planning range is RMB 350–650 for budget travel, RMB 800–1,500 for mid-range travel, or RMB 1,800–3,000+ for comfortable travel, excluding international flights and major intercity journeys.

faqs.question: Do I need to book attractions in advance?
faqs.answer: Check and reserve capacity-controlled attractions before travel. The Palace Museum and Terracotta Warriors should be verified through official channels, especially for weekends and peak periods.

faqs.question: Can ChinaEase Buddy adjust this route to my flights?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your dates, arrival and departure cities, flight times, group size, interests, pace, and practical concerns to receive a route built around your real trip.
